chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa or someone else, from Qutayba ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is upon you with (eating) the celery, for it is a food of Ilyas (peace be upon him), and Al-Yas'a (peace be upon him), and Yoshua ibn Noun (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of eating celery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophetic tradition of dietary wisdom by linking celery to the sustenance of key prophets, specifically Ilyas (Elijah), Al-Yas'a (Elisha), and Yoshua ibn Noun (Joshua). In Shia scholarly tradition, this connection underscores the continuity of divine guidance through physical nourishment, validating the health benefits of celery as a legacy of righteous predecessors. The mention of these specific figures emphasizes the spiritual and physical purity associated with their respective missions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, or someone else, from Quteyba Bin Mihran, from Hammad Bin Zakariyya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the celery, for it is a food of Ilyas<sup>as</sup>, and Al-Yas’a<sup>as</sup>, and Yoshua<sup>as</sup> Bin Noun<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa or others from Qutaybah ibn Mehran from Hammad ibn Zakariya who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You must eat celery because it is the food of Elias, al-Yasa‘ and Usha‘ ibn Nun (names of Israelite prophets).”’
